gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Shokz's own US store sells the OpenMeet, a bone-conduction office headset, for $119.95 today (marked down from $249.95). That undercuts both of ChatGPT's call picks: the OpenComm2 (2025) at $159.95 and the OpenComm2 UC at $199.95.
standout_why: Openear Club's 'Best Bone Conduction Headphones With Mic' page lists the OpenComm2 UC ($199.95), OpenRun Pro 2 ($179.95), OpenRun Air 2 ($129.95), Suunto Wing 2 ($179.00), OpenSwim Pro ($229.95) and OpenRun ($129.95). It doesn't mention the OpenMeet at all. SoundGuys' best-list (dated 2026-01-23) picks the OpenMeet UC as 'The best for the office' but prices it at $179.95 at Amazon (MSRP $249.95), which is $60 above today's Shokz price. The four RTINGS pages and Tom's Guide returned only navigation, not article text, when opened, so I couldn't check what they state. ChatGPT's answer never showed the OpenMeet on a card. Not 3 because I couldn't open the OpenMeet product page (HTTP 429), so I haven't confirmed whether the $119.95 listing includes the Loop120 USB adapter (the UC kit).
decides: On price, it changes the value pick for calls. The OpenMeet has a dual-mic system (Shokz claims up to 98.6% noise reduction), DualPitch drivers and up to 15 hours of battery for $119.95, which is $40 less than the OpenComm2 (2025) and $80 less than the OpenComm2 UC. If the $119.95 listing turns out to be the UC kit with the adapter, it beats the OpenComm2 UC for Zoom/Teams use at $80 less. Otherwise it still beats the OpenComm2 for phone calls on price. ChatGPT's split between OpenComm2 for calls and OpenRun Pro 2 for exercise holds. Of our own products, the MOJAWA Run Plus ($99.99) is a sports/swim set and doesn't compete for calls.
